title: The present subjunctive: forms (que trabaje, que viva)
summary: A new mood for wishes, feelings and the not-yet-real: build all six present subjunctive forms and use them after ojalá.
focus: Forming the present subjunctive (regular, spelling-change and irregular verbs) and using it after ojalá
content:
## Two moods, facts and the not-yet-real

A **mood** shows how the speaker sees an action. So far you have used the **indicative**: facts, things you know, things that happen. The **subjunctive** (**el subjuntivo**) is for what is not real yet: wishes, feelings, doubts, requests.

- **Mi hermano trabaja mucho.** My brother works a lot. (A fact, so indicative.)
- **Ojalá mi hermano trabaje menos.** I hope my brother works less. (A wish, so subjunctive.)

You have met it already: **usted** commands (**hable**, **coma**) and negative commands (**no hables**) are subjunctive forms. This lesson builds all six forms. The next lessons add the triggers that call for them.

## Building it: the opposite vowel

Take the **yo** form of the present, drop the **-o** and add the "opposite" vowel: **-ar** verbs take **-e**, **-er / -ir** verbs take **-a**.

| | trabajar | aprender | vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | trabaje | aprenda | viva |
| tú | trabajes | aprendas | vivas |
| él / ella / usted | trabaje | aprenda | viva |
| nosotros/as | trabajemos | aprendamos | vivamos |
| vosotros/as | trabajéis | aprendáis | viváis |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | trabajen | aprendan | vivan |

**Yo** and **él** share one form. An irregular **yo** carries into every person: tengo → **tenga**, hago → **haga**, salgo → **salga**.

## Spelling: busque, llegue, empiece

The new vowel would change the sound of the last consonant, so the spelling changes to keep it, in all six forms:

| ending | change | example |
|---|---|---|
| -car | c → qu | buscar → **busque**, busquemos |
| -gar | g → gu | llegar → **llegue**, lleguemos |
| -zar | z → c | empezar → **empiece**, empecemos |

- **Ojalá el autobús llegue pronto.** (I hope the bus comes soon.)
- **Ojalá busquéis un piso juntos.** (I hope you look for a flat together.)

**Empezar** also keeps its **e → ie** change (empiece, but empecemos). Stem changers are the next lesson.

## The irregulars: dé, esté, haya, sepa, vea

**Dar**, **estar**, **haber** and **saber** do not follow the **yo** rule. **Ver** does (veo → **vea**), but it is listed with them for reference.

| | dar | estar | haber | saber | ver |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yo | dé | esté | haya | sepa | vea |
| tú | des | estés | hayas | sepas | veas |
| él / ella | dé | esté | haya | sepa | vea |
| nosotros | demos | estemos | hayamos | sepamos | veamos |
| vosotros | deis | estéis | hayáis | sepáis | veáis |
| ellos / ellas | den | estén | hayan | sepan | vean |

From the imperative you already know **ser → sea** and **ir → vaya**. Accents matter: **dé** (give) vs **de** (of), and **esté** vs **este** (this). **Haya** is the subjunctive of **hay**. Haya + participle comes at B2.

## The first trigger: ojalá

**Ojalá** means *I hope* or *if only*, and it is always followed by the subjunctive. It never changes form, and a **que** after it is optional.

- **Ojalá haga sol el sábado.** (I hope it's sunny on Saturday.)
- **Ojalá que estés mejor pronto.** (I hope you're better soon.)
- **Ojalá no haya cola en el museo.** (I hope there's no queue at the museum.)
- **¡Ojalá!** I hope so! / Let's hope so!

With the present subjunctive, **ojalá** is a wish that can still come true. Ojalá for unlikely wishes (with the imperfect subjunctive) comes at B2.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá tengas suerte en el examen.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope you're lucky in the exam.

vocabulary.meaning: the subjunctive (the mood of wishes, feelings and doubt)
vocabulary.example: El subjuntivo de estar lleva tilde: esté.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The subjunctive of estar has a written accent: esté.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá mi madre no trabaje este domingo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope my mother isn't working this Sunday.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá aprendáis mucho en Salamanca.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope you all learn a lot in Salamanca.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá vivamos cerca algún día.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we live close to each other one day.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá estés mejor mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope you're better tomorrow.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá me den el trabajo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope they give me the job.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá sepas la respuesta.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope you know the answer.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá haya plazas en el tren de las ocho.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope there are seats on the eight o'clock train.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá veamos el mar desde la habitación.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we can see the sea from the room.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá Ana busque un piso en el centro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope Ana looks for a flat in the centre.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el tren llegue a tiempo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the train arrives on time.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá las vacaciones empiecen pronto.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the holidays start soon.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá mi padre ___ (trabajar) menos este año.
quiz.explanation: -ar verbs take -e in the subjunctive: trabajo → trabaje. Ojalá always takes the subjunctive.
hints: Start from 'trabajo', drop the -o, add the opposite vowel.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá (nosotros) ___ juntos en Barcelona algún día.
quiz.explanation: -ir verbs take -a in the subjunctive: vivamos. 'Vivimos' is the indicative, and 'vivemos' does not exist.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá mi vuelo ___ antes de las diez.
quiz.explanation: -gar verbs add a u to keep the hard g sound: llegue. 'Llege' would sound like 'lleje', and 'llega' is the indicative.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá el concierto ___ (empezar) a las nueve.
quiz.explanation: -zar verbs change z → c before e, and empezar keeps its e → ie change: empiece.
Being well is a state, so estar, and after ojalá it goes into the subjunctive: estén, with an accent.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá el profesor nos ___ más tiempo para el examen.
quiz.explanation: The subjunctive of dar is dé, with an accent to tell it apart from the preposition 'de'. 'Da' is the indicative.
hints: The give-verb needs an accent here.

quiz.explanation: Saber has an irregular subjunctive: sepa, sepas, sepa, sepamos, sepáis, sepan.
hints: Not from 'sé': the stem is sep-.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá ___ (haber: hay) entradas para el concierto del sábado.
quiz.explanation: The subjunctive of 'hay' is 'haya', the same for one thing or many: ojalá haya entradas.
hints: What is the subjunctive of hay?
It doesn't change for plural nouns.

conversations.title: The night before the interview
conversations.scenario: Diego has a job interview tomorrow, and his friend Lucía calls to wish him luck.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Mañana tengo la entrevista en la editorial. Estoy nerviosísimo.
lines.meaning: Tomorrow I have the interview at the publisher's. I'm really nervous.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Ojalá te den el puesto! Te lo mereces.
lines.meaning: I hope they give you the job! You deserve it.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ojalá. Pero no sé si sé bastante inglés.
lines.meaning: Let's hope so. But I don't know if I know enough English.
lines.note: ¡Ojalá! on its own means let's hope so

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Seguro que sí. Ojalá la entrevistadora vea toda tu experiencia.
lines.meaning: I'm sure you do. I hope the interviewer sees all your experience.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Y ojalá no haya mucho tráfico, porque la oficina está lejos.
lines.meaning: And I hope there isn't much traffic, because the office is far away.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sal temprano. Ojalá el autobús llegue puntual.
lines.meaning: Leave early. Let's hope the bus is on time.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Si me lo dan, ¿lo celebramos el sábado?
lines.meaning: If they give it to me, shall we celebrate on Saturday?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¡Claro! Ojalá estemos todos: tú, yo y tu hermana.
lines.meaning: Of course! I hope we're all there: you, me and your sister.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Let's hope so. She's working a lot lately.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Pues ojalá trabaje menos esa semana. ¡Mucha suerte mañana!
lines.meaning: Well, hopefully she works less that week. Good luck tomorrow!

listening.text: Ojalá haga buen tiempo.
listening.meaning: I hope the weather is good.
listening.note: Hago becomes haga because the yo stem carries over.

listening.text: Ojalá mi hermana viva más cerca.
listening.meaning: I hope my sister comes to live closer.
listening.note: Vivir becomes viva because -ir verbs take -a.

listening.text: Ojalá veamos a los abuelos este domingo.
listening.meaning: I hope we see our grandparents this Sunday.

listening.text: Ojalá el jefe nos dé el viernes libre.
listening.meaning: I hope the boss gives us Friday off.
listening.note: Dé carries an accent because it is the verb, not 'de'.

listening.text: Ojalá que mis amigos estén en casa esta noche.
listening.meaning: I hope my friends are at home tonight.
listening.note: The que after ojalá is optional.

listening.text: Ojalá Pablo sepa la dirección de la oficina nueva.
listening.meaning: I hope Pablo knows the address of the new office.
listening.note: New word: la dirección = the address.

listening.text: Ojalá los niños busquen las llaves antes de salir de casa.
listening.meaning: I hope the children look for the keys before leaving home.
listening.note: Buscar becomes busquen: c turns into qu.

listening.text: Ojalá mi compañero de piso trabaje menos horas en la fábrica.
listening.meaning: I hope my flatmate works fewer hours at the factory.
listening.note: New word: la fábrica = the factory.

guide.tip: A fact takes the indicative (trabaja). A wish, a hope or anything not yet real takes the subjunctive (trabaje). Ojalá always takes the subjunctive.

bites.title: Fact or not-yet-real?
bites.rule: The indicative is for facts and what you know. The subjunctive is for wishes, feelings and doubt, anything that isn't real yet.
bites.example_meaning: He works a lot. I hope he works less.

bites.title: The opposite vowel
bites.rule: Take the yo form, drop -o and swap the vowel. -ar verbs take -e (trabaje), and -er/-ir verbs take -a (aprenda, viva).
bites.example_meaning: I hope you learn a lot.

bites.title: Keep the sound
bites.rule: Before e, -car becomes qu, -gar becomes gu and -zar becomes c: busque, llegue, empiece.
bites.example_meaning: I hope the train arrives soon.

bites.title: The irregulars
bites.rule: dé, esté, haya, sepa, vea, plus sea and vaya. Dé and esté carry accents.
bites.example: Ojalá haya sitio y esté abierto.
bites.example_meaning: I hope there's room and it's open.

sorts.title: Fact or wish?

items.text: Ojalá haya sitio en el tren.

sorts.why: A fact you state takes the indicative; after ojalá the same verb turns subjunctive.

sorts.title: Which vowel in the subjunctive?
sorts.why: -ar verbs (estar too: esté) switch to -e; -er and -ir verbs (ver gives vea, saber gives sepa) switch to -a.

spots.sentence: Ojalá mi jefe me da un día libre.
spots.why: After ojalá comes the subjunctive. Dar becomes dé, with an accent.

spots.sentence: Ojalá que no hay mucha gente en la playa.
spots.why: The subjunctive of hay is haya.
Ojalá takes the subjunctive, and -car becomes qu: busque.

builds.meaning: I hope you learn a lot this year.
I hope my parents live nearby.

builds.text: Ojalá el profesor nos dé más tiempo.
builds.meaning: I hope the teacher gives us more time.
I hope you know the truth.

realm.content:
## Ojalá en Eldmark

Before every raid the guild makes wishes, and wishes take the subjunctive. For example **ojalá el paladín esté listo**, **ojalá haya botín**, **ojalá la maga sepa el hechizo**, **ojalá el rey nos dé una recompensa**. Facts stay indicative: **el enano trabaja en Deepanvil**.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá ganemos la batalla de Frostmarch.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we win the battle of Frostmarch.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el paladín esté listo para la banda.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the paladin is ready for the raid.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá haya botín en el cofre.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope there's loot in the chest.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá la maga sepa abrir el portal.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the mage knows how to open the portal.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el rey de Highgate nos dé una recompensa.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the king of Highgate gives us a reward.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá no veamos ningún dragón en el Bosque Umbrío.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we don't see any dragon in the Bosque Umbrío.

vocabulary.example: El botín de hoy es una espada vieja.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Today's loot is an old sword.

vocabulary.example: La elfa aprende un hechizo nuevo.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The elf learns a new spell.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá mi montura llegue antes que la tuya.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope my mount gets there before yours.

bites.title: Deseos de aventurero
bites.rule: Every adventurer's wish starts with ojalá and takes the subjunctive (esté, haya, sepa, dé, vea). Facts about the realm stay indicative.
bites.example: Ojalá haya botín en la mazmorra.
bites.example_meaning: I hope there's loot in the dungeon.

listening.text: Ojalá ganemos el torneo de Highgate.
listening.meaning: I hope we win the Highgate tournament.
listening.note: New word: el torneo = the tournament.

listening.text: Ojalá el enano trabaje en la forja.
listening.meaning: I hope the dwarf works at the forge.
listening.note: New word: la forja = the forge.

listening.text: Ojalá los elfos vean el humo.
listening.meaning: I hope the elves see the smoke.

listening.text: Ojalá el orco no sepa nuestro plan.
listening.meaning: I hope the orc doesn't know our plan.

listening.text: Ojalá la maga aprenda el hechizo a tiempo.
listening.meaning: I hope the mage learns the spell in time.

builds.meaning: I hope the paladin is ready.
I hope we get to live in Emberhold.

spots.sentence: Ojalá el cazador ve al lobo.
Ojalá la maga sabe el hechizo.
spots.why: The subjunctive of saber is sepa.

sorts.title: ¿Hecho o deseo?

items.text: La elfa vive en el Bosque Umbrío.

sorts.why: What is true in the realm takes the indicative; what the guild hopes for takes the subjunctive after ojalá.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá el rey nos ___ una recompensa.
quiz.explanation: Ojalá takes the subjunctive: dar becomes dé, with an accent to tell it from 'de'.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá (nosotros) ___ (ver) el castillo de Highgate mañana.
quiz.explanation: Ver keeps the e of veo: vea, veas, vea, veamos.

conversations.title: Before the raid
conversations.scenario: Brunilda the dwarf warrior and Ilvan the elf mage wait at the dungeon gate.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Are you ready for the dungeon, Ilvan?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Casi. Ojalá sepa todos los hechizos.
lines.meaning: Almost. I hope I know all the spells.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Y ojalá haya mucho botín esta vez.
lines.meaning: And I hope there's a lot of loot this time.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Ojalá el jefe no nos vea llegar.
lines.meaning: I hope the boss doesn't see us coming.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Tranquilo. Ojalá el paladín esté despierto, eso sí.
lines.meaning: Relax. I do hope the paladin is awake, though.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Ojalá! La última vez durmió encima de su montura.
lines.meaning: Let's hope so! Last time he fell asleep on his mount.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vamos. Ojalá lleguemos a Highgate antes de la cena.
lines.meaning: Let's go. I hope we get back to Highgate before dinner.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Y ojalá el posadero nos dé sopa caliente.
lines.meaning: And I hope the innkeeper gives us hot soup.

meadowbrook.content:
## Ojalá en la granja

Farm life runs on hopes. For example **ojalá haga sol**, **ojalá las fresas estén maduras**, **ojalá Leo vea muchos peces en el río**, **ojalá el alcalde nos dé un premio en el festival**. A fact (**Rosa trabaja en la tienda**) stays indicative, and a hope takes the subjunctive.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá haga buen tiempo en primavera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the weather is good in spring.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá Nora no trabaje sola en la mina.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope Nora doesn't work alone in the mine.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá las fresas estén maduras el lunes.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the strawberries are ripe on Monday.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá Leo vea un pez grande en el río.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope Leo sees a big fish in the river.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el alcalde me dé el premio de la calabaza.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the mayor gives me the pumpkin prize.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá aprenda a cuidar las vacas este año.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope I learn to look after the cows this year.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá la cosecha sea buena este otoño.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the harvest is good this autumn.

vocabulary.example: El premio del festival es una medalla.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The festival prize is a medal.

vocabulary.example: El maíz ya está maduro.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The corn is already ripe.

bites.title: Ojalá en la granja
bites.rule: Hopes for the farm take ojalá and the subjunctive, as in ojalá haga sol, ojalá las vacas estén bien, ojalá Rosa tenga semillas.
bites.example_meaning: I hope the harvest is good.

listening.text: Ojalá Rosa tenga semillas de maíz.
listening.meaning: I hope Rosa has corn seeds.
listening.note: New word: las semillas = the seeds.

listening.text: Ojalá las gallinas estén en el gallinero.
listening.meaning: I hope the hens are in the hen house.

listening.meaning: I hope Leo gives us a fish.

listening.text: Ojalá Nora sepa plantar calabazas.
listening.meaning: I hope Nora knows how to plant pumpkins.

listening.text: Ojalá veamos fuegos artificiales en el festival.
listening.meaning: I hope we see fireworks at the festival.

builds.meaning: I hope the harvest is good.
I hope Leo sees lots of fish.

spots.sentence: Ojalá el alcalde me da el premio.
spots.why: After ojalá: dé, with an accent.

sorts.title: -e or -a?
sorts.why: -ar farm verbs take -e (plante, coseche); -er and -ir verbs take -a (venda, viva).

quiz.explanation: -ar verbs take -e in the subjunctive: planto → plante.
hints: Ojalá takes the subjunctive, and -ar verbs take -e.

quiz.prompt: Ojalá ___ sol el día del festival.
quiz.explanation: Ojalá takes the subjunctive; hacer builds it from hago: haga.
hints: The yo stem hag- carries over.

rustwake.content:
## Ojalá en el páramo

Out in **el páramo** every plan ends in a hope. For example **ojalá no haya tormenta de ceniza**, **ojalá Marta tenga agua filtrada**, **ojalá el radiorreloj esté arreglado**, **ojalá el robot jardinero sepa volver**. What you know is indicative; what you hope is subjunctive.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá encontremos tuercas en la gasolinera.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we find nuts at the petrol station.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá no haya polvo mañana.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope there's no dust tomorrow.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá el radiorreloj esté arreglado.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope the wrist radio is fixed.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá Leo el buscador sepa el camino.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope Leo the scavenger knows the way.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá busquemos en el centro comercial en ruinas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we search the ruined shopping centre.

vocabulary.example: Ojalá vivamos fuera de la cúpula algún día.
vocabulary.example_meaning: I hope we live outside the Dome one day.

vocabulary.example: Marta acepta tuercas por el agua.
vocabulary.example_meaning: Marta accepts nuts for the water.

vocabulary.example: El páramo es enorme y seco.
vocabulary.example_meaning: The barren plains are huge and dry.

vocabulary.example: Mi radiorreloj funciona otra vez.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My wrist radio works again.

bites.title: Ojalá en el páramo
bites.rule: Out in the wasteland, hopes take ojalá and the subjunctive, as in ojalá haya agua, ojalá el radiorreloj funcione, ojalá Ruiz esté contento.
bites.example: Ojalá no haya una tormenta de ceniza.
bites.example_meaning: I hope there isn't an ash storm.

sorts.title: ¿Hecho o esperanza?

quiz.prompt: Ojalá Leo el buscador ___ el camino al taller.
quiz.explanation: Saber is irregular in the subjunctive: sepa. 'Sabe' is the indicative; 'sepe' does not exist.
-car verbs change c → qu before e: busquemos.
hints: Keep the hard c sound: qu.
